resolvedQuestions.text: Which fixture setup, waits, subprocesses, and assertions account for the roughly 400-second cli lane in tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and what test-only changes can reduce elapsed time while retaining every assertion?
Which of the 12 serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution, and what would shrink that group?
What sets the time of the cli lane's tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and can it be cut without dropping assertions?
Which twelve timing-sensitive system-deep-loop files make up about 265 seconds, what shared-state or timing assumptions keep them serial, and can any safe scheduling change retain all assertions?
What accounts for about 300 seconds of import time in the spec-kit core lane, how is that time produced, and which test-process or module-loading changes can reduce it without changing coverage?
Where do the roughly 300 s of import time in the spec-kit core lane come from, and which parts can be cut?
Do the ledger read-caching ideas (singleWriterReadCache, gateway rescans) buy measurable time, and what runtime risk do they carry?
What evidence would justify production changes involving singleWriterReadCache or gateway rescans, and how should their runtime-behavior risk be separated from test-only speed work?
How do worker count and file parallelism affect elapsed time on smaller CI runners, and what runner-specific measurements should guide any concurrency change?
Which remaining cuts still pay off on a smaller CI runner, and how should each be measured before it is claimed as a win?

keyFindings.text: The upgrade-legacy file is a stateful integration suite: its main describes reset a shared sandbox after cases, and each reset performs a hard Git reset, removes fixture trees, recreates `specs/`, and restamps copied `dist` files; `beforeAll` also recursively copies the skill and creates a committed temporary repository. These are plausible costs, but no per-case profile attributes the supplied 400 seconds to them. The file's dominant work is process creation, not computation: 74 `runUpgrade` call sites each spawn `node .../upgrade-legacy.mjs`, and every packet validation inside that CLI spawns `bash validate.sh`, which spawns two more node processes — one for the dist-freshness check and one for the validation orchestrator. keyFindings.text: Vitest's reported `import` time is a sum over files, not wall time: the summary line computes `collectTime = sum(files, file => file.collectDuration)` and prints it beside the wall `executionTime`. A 300 s import figure therefore cannot be read as 300 s of wall clock, which matters for the packet's framing of the core lane. `[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.UpGiHP7g.js:2465]` `[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.UpGiHP7g.js:2474]`

keyFindings.text: The one structural lever this file offers is sharding, not trimming: 58 self-resetting tests can move into separate files, each with its own sandbox, and Vitest already runs cli files in parallel. The copy cost is paid once per shard (about 35.8 MB), while the per-test process work parallelises. A 4-shard split is an estimate of roughly 400 s down to 120-150 s wall on this machine, and it must be measured, not claimed. `[INFERENCE: from findings 2, 4 and 6 plus the cli project's fileParallelism: true at .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/vitest.config.ts:57]`

This is a no-code baseline route for lane-level measurements, but the CLI Vitest helper itself only reports success/failure for its two concurrent processes.
